articles.authors: Small C, Kumar D, Abbas A, Sánchez Fructuoso A, Yamanaga S et al.
articles.title: AS01E-adjuvanted RSV pre-F protein vaccine in adults with lung or kidney transplant: a phase 2b randomized trial.
articles.summary: Phase 2b open-label randomized trial evaluating the immunogenicity and safety of AS01E-adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccine in kidney or lung transplant recipients receiving one (n=131) or two doses (n=130) versus non-immunocompromised controls ≥50 years (n=125). A second dose increased RSV-A and RSV-B neutralizing antibody titers (mean geometric increases 1.34 and 1.26), with responses sustained over 12 months.

pico.population: Kidney or lung transplant recipients aged ≥18 years (and non-immunocompromised controls aged ≥50 years).
pico.intervention: Two doses of AS01E-adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccine 30-60 days apart (or single dose).
pico.comparison: Single dose of AS01E-adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccine in transplant recipients, or single dose in non-immunocompromised controls.
pico.outcome: Primary: Mean geometric increase in RSV-A and RSV-B neutralizing titers 1 month post-dose 2 relative to dose 1 in transplant recipients. Secondary: Safety and immunogenicity compared with controls.

inclusion: Kidney or lung transplant recipients aged ≥18 years

appraisal.bottom_line: A two-dose regimen of AS01E-adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccine in kidney and lung transplant recipients increased neutralizing antibody titers against RSV-A (mean geometric increase 1.34, 95% CI 1.20-1.48) and RSV-B (mean geometric increase 1.26, 95% CI 1.14-1.40) post-second dose, with humoral and cellular responses persisting for 12 months and an acceptable safety profile.
appraisal.relevance: Solid organ transplant recipients are at high risk for severe RSV complications; these data show that a two-dose strategy induces better immunogenicity than a single dose, particularly in patients on mycophenolate.
appraisal.caveat: Open-label phase 2b trial evaluated surrogate immunogenicity metrics (neutralizing antibody titers and CD4+ T-cell counts) rather than clinical efficacy endpoints such as laboratory-confirmed RSV infection or hospitalizations.

articles.authors: Banerjee D, Ali M, Tumelty E, Murphy D, Warrens H et al.
articles.title: Rapid Renin Angiotensin Aldosterone System inhibitor optimisation in patients with chronic kidney disease and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction using potassium binder: a randomised, double-blinded, placebo-controlled trial.
articles.summary: Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial evaluating sodium zirconium cyclosilicate (SZC) versus placebo in 112 patients with CKD stages 3-5 and HFrEF with serum potassium 5.0-5.5 mmol/L to facilitate RAASi up-titration over 14 weeks. SZC significantly increased the proportion of patients reaching target RAASi dose without hyperkalemia (56% vs 28%, ITT OR 3.16).

pico.population: Patients with HFrEF, CKD stages 3-5, and serum potassium 5.0-5.5 mmol/L (n=112).
pico.outcome: Achieving target RAASi dose without developing hyperkalemia (serum potassium ≥5.6 mmol/L) over 14 weeks.

appraisal.bottom_line: Co-administration of SZC allowed more patients with CKD 3-5 and HFrEF to achieve target RAASi doses without developing hyperkalemia over 14 weeks compared with placebo (56% vs 28% in per-protocol analysis, p=0.006; ITT OR 3.16, 95% CI 1.35-7.39, p=0.008).
appraisal.relevance: Hyperkalemia is the main barrier to optimizing evidence-based RAASi therapy in patients with combined heart failure and advanced CKD; potassium binders offer a potential strategy to enable guideline-directed medical therapy.
appraisal.caveat: Small sample size (112 total randomized; 96 completed per-protocol analysis) and short duration (14 weeks) evaluating a composite surrogate endpoint of medication titration and serum potassium rather than clinical cardiovascular or renal outcomes. Funded by AstraZeneca.

articles.authors: de Oliveira AN, Aguiar PEG, Babadopoulos YD, Alves MVS, da Cruz Júnior JL et al.
articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy and prognostic value of urinary soluble CD163 in lupus nephritis: a systematic review and diagnostic meta-analysis : Urinary sCD163 for active lupus nephritis.
articles.summary: Systematic review and diagnostic meta-analysis of 8 studies (1,110 participants) evaluating urinary soluble CD163 (uCD163) for identifying active lupus nephritis. Pooled sensitivity was 0.89 and specificity was 0.91, with an SROC AUC of 0.93.

pico.population: Patients with systemic lupus erythematosus being evaluated for active lupus nephritis (8 studies, n=1,110).
pico.comparison: Renal biopsy or standard clinical diagnostic criteria for active lupus nephritis.
pico.outcome: Diagnostic performance parameters: sensitivity, specificity, diagnostic odds ratio (DOR), and area under the SROC curve (AUC).

inclusion: Studies evaluating the performance of uCD163 in detecting active lupus nephritis in patients with SLE

appraisal.bottom_line: Urinary soluble CD163 demonstrated strong diagnostic accuracy for active lupus nephritis, with a pooled sensitivity of 0.89 (95% CI 0.79-0.94), pooled specificity of 0.91 (95% CI 0.81-0.96), pooled DOR of 63.37 (95% CI 14.25-281.75), and SROC AUC of 0.93.
appraisal.relevance: Noninvasive urinary biomarkers that accurately mirror active renal macrophage activation could reduce reliance on repeat kidney biopsies for monitoring lupus nephritis flares.
appraisal.caveat: High between-study heterogeneity (I² = 85%) and potential publication bias/small-study effects (Deeks' test p=0.0995); optimal diagnostic cutoffs were not standardized across studies, and overall certainty of evidence was graded as low.

articles.authors: Kumar S, Loganathan S, Kajal K, Gandhi K, Sethi S et al.
articles.title: Comparison of the effects of normal saline versus Plasma-Lyte® on acid-base balance during living donor kidney transplantation surgery using goal-directed fluid therapy based on pulse pressure variation- a randomised controlled trial.
articles.summary: Prospective, assessor-blinded randomized trial comparing intraoperative normal saline (NS, n=55) vs Plasma-Lyte (PL, n=56) using PPV-guided goal-directed fluid therapy in 111 living donor kidney transplant recipients. There was no statistically significant difference in apparent strong ion difference (SIDa) at end of surgery (adjusted difference 0.71 mmol/L), though formal equivalence was not met.

pico.population: Adult patients undergoing living donor kidney transplantation (n=111).
pico.comparison: 0.9% Normal Saline (NS) titrated via PPV-guided algorithm (n=55).
pico.outcome: Primary: Adjusted difference in apparent strong ion difference (SIDa) at end of surgery. Secondary: SIDe, SIG, pH, potassium, lactate, delayed graft function, and serum creatinine trends.

inclusion: Adult patients undergoing living donor kidney transplantation

appraisal.bottom_line: When intraoperative fluid is administered via a pulse pressure variation (PPV)-guided algorithm, Normal Saline and Plasma-Lyte yielded similar acid-base outcomes at end of surgery (adjusted SIDa difference 0.71 mmol/L, 90% CI -0.90 to +2.32 mmol/L; p=0.46), though formal equivalence within ±2 mmol/L was not statistically proven.
appraisal.relevance: Hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis from normal saline is a major concern in kidney transplantation; this trial suggests that delivering moderate fluid volumes (~1.8-1.9 L) guided by dynamic hemodynamic protocols may attenuate major acid-base disparities regardless of crystalloid type.
appraisal.caveat: Failed to establish formal statistical equivalence for the primary endpoint; single-center trial with a small sample size (n=111) that was underpowered to detect clinical differences in graft function outcomes such as DGF or early graft dysfunction.

articles.authors: Tesfaw LM, Dalugoda Y, Tiong MK, Osborne NJ, Williams GM et al.
articles.title: Geographical disparities and temporal trends of end stage kidney disease incidence: a systematic review.
articles.summary: Systematic review of 41 original studies assessing geographic variations and temporal trends in ESKD incidence globally over two decades. ESKD incidence varied widely across countries (100 per million in Nepal to >450 per million in Taiwan) and exhibited increasing temporal trends in most regions.

pico.population: Adults aged ≥18 years with end-stage kidney disease globally (41 studies).
pico.intervention: Geographical location (country, region, small areas) or time period (annual, seasonal).
pico.outcome: ESKD incidence rates, geographical disparities, and temporal trends.

inclusion: Original studies published between 01 Jan 2003 and 23 Mar 2026
Focus on ESKD incidence in adults (≥18 years)
Reporting geographical variations and/or temporal trends

appraisal.bottom_line: ESKD incidence shows broad global variation ranging from 100 per million in Nepal to >450 per million in Taiwan, with significant small-area intra-country clustering and a general upward temporal trajectory globally.
appraisal.relevance: Synthesizing geographical and temporal epidemiology highlights environmental, systemic, and healthcare access factors influencing kidney disease progression, supporting targeted preventive strategies.
appraisal.caveat: Systematic review summarizing heterogeneous observational and ecological studies; identified associations (e.g., ACEi use, EPO use, paraquat exposure) represent population-level correlates rather than proven causal mechanisms.

articles.authors: Zeng CM, Liu GQ, Lin H, Cai L, Huang CZ et al.
articles.title: Enhanced External Counterpulsation Reduces the Risk of Early Cystatin-C Rise in STEMI Patients After Primary PCI: A Single-Center Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial.
articles.summary: Single-center randomized trial evaluating enhanced external counterpulsation (EECP) initiated within 4-12 hours post-primary PCI for up to 72 hours in 436 STEMI patients (211 EECP vs 225 control). EECP significantly reduced post-PCI cystatin-C rise (OR 0.44), but showed no significant reduction in serum creatinine-defined contrast-induced AKI (p=0.584).

pico.intervention: Enhanced external counterpulsation (EECP) for up to 72 hours post-PCI plus routine care (n=211).
pico.outcome: Cystatin-C levels, risk of cystatin-C rise, post-PCI eGFR, serum creatinine, and SCr-defined contrast-induced AKI (CI-AKI).

appraisal.bottom_line: Adjunctive EECP therapy after primary PCI in STEMI patients reduced the risk of early cystatin-C elevation (OR 0.44, 95% CI 0.19-0.94, p=0.034), but did not significantly alter the incidence of serum creatinine-defined contrast-induced AKI (p=0.584).
appraisal.relevance: Non-pharmacological strategies to mitigate acute kidney injury after urgent cardiac catheterization are needed; however, biomarker efficacy must translate into clinical AKI endpoints.
appraisal.caveat: Single-center unblinded trial where the primary positive finding was limited to a surrogate serum biomarker (cystatin-C elevation risk), while clinical SCr-defined AKI rates were not significantly reduced.
